claims.statement: Dogs Trust explains that reactive dogs bark, lunge and pull toward triggers but this is not always aggression; behaviour expresses how the dog feels and can become a learned habit that can change with training and support.
claims.confidenceJustification: Explicit framing on charity guidance page.

claims.statement: Dogs Trust advises having a reactive dog examined by a vet to check for underlying medical conditions before behaviour change work, noting pain and illness can reduce tolerance and coping.
Dogs Trust immediate reactivity guidance: increase distance until the dog relaxes, then reward with praise, food or a favourite toy; avoid telling the dog off because this can increase stress.
limitations: Management not full behaviour modification plan.

claims.statement: Dogs Trust advises keeping the lead secure but relaxed during reactive moments, because tension on the lead can make a dog feel trapped and worsen reactions.
Dogs Trust states stress hormone levels can take 48–72 hours to drop after a reactive episode, during which the dog may remain agitated and more trigger-sensitive.
claims.confidenceJustification: Charity education statement; cite as management heuristic not primary physiology claim.
limitations: Individual variation; not a controlled study in this source.

claims.statement: Dogs Trust offers a Behaviour Support Line and may recommend further behaviour support when phone advice is insufficient.
RSPCA teaches 'leave' by waiting for the dog to back off from a treat in a closed fist, then opening the hand to release the treat and praise—building that disengaging is rewarded.
limitations: Teaches disengagement from hand-held item; not mouth 'drop' cue alone.

claims.statement: RSPCA instructs adding the cue word 'leave' in a gentle tone as the dog backs off, before releasing the treat.

As of batch 004 retrieval (2026-10-10), RSPCA dog training index lists sit, lie down, stay and leave pages; no dedicated public 'drop/give' training URL was found—owners should pair RSPCA leave with Dogs Trust leave/fair-trade guidance for item release.
claims.confidenceJustification: HTTP 404 on candidate drop URLs; training hub link crawl.

claims.statement: Dogs Trust states the first four months are a vital socialisation window when puppies learn what is normal, requiring gradual positive introductions to people, dogs, noises, objects and experiences.

Dogs Trust advises puppies should not walk on public ground before full vaccination, but can be carried (carrier/sling) to begin socialisation experiences until the vet confirms it is safe to go on the ground.
limitations: Follow individual vet protocol on timing.

claims.statement: Dogs Trust instructs stopping socialisation interactions immediately if the puppy shows high arousal or signs of becoming worried or frightened, because negative or overwhelming early experiences increase later behaviour problems.
claims.excerptOrParaphrase: Stop if worried; quality over quantity.

claims.statement: Dogs Trust Puppy 101 hub advises going at the individual puppy's pace and using rewards they like for kind, positive learning rather than a one-size-fits-all checklist.

Verbeek et al. (2024) scoping review of 706 human–dog bond publications (2012–2023) reports dog training as a recurring behavioural welfare theme (≈9.5% of behaviour-domain welfare issues), synthesising reward- versus aversive-method discussions including Vieira de Castro protocol overview.
claims.excerptOrParaphrase: Training listed among top behavioural welfare topics.
claims.confidenceJustification: Scoping review mapping literature, not new RCT data.

claims.statement: Verbeek et al. (2024) note most reviewed human–dog bond welfare research involves pet dogs from WEIRD societies, limiting global generalisation.

The 2024 systematic review of counterconditioning-based dog behaviour interventions (14 studies) reports mostly positive outcomes for some kennel and dog–dog or visitor aggression contexts, but separation-related problems were more resistant and definitions of counterconditioning varied across studies.
claims.excerptOrParaphrase: Heterogeneous CC methods; mixed behaviour outcomes.
claims.confidenceJustification: Small-n systematic review; abstract-level KB entry.

protocols.title: Leave — fist closed progression (RSPCA)
protocols.intendedOutcome: Dog disengages from presented item on gentle 'leave' cue.
inappropriateWhen: Resource guarding with bite risk—refer to behaviourist

steps.instruction: Place treat in closed fist; say 'take it' in friendly voice and let dog sniff/lick closed hand without opening.
steps.rewardTiming: No reward until dog backs off.
steps.progressCriteria: Dog learns closed fist does not release on mouthing.
steps.easierIfStruggling: Use lower-value treat in fist; higher-value reward when opening hand.
failureModes: Opening fist while dog is mouthing

steps.instruction: When dog backs off even slightly, open fist, release treat and praise generously.
steps.easierIfStruggling: Wait for larger gap if needed.
failureModes: Rewarding while nose still on fist

steps.instruction: Add gentle 'leave' as dog backs off, then release treat; progress to treat visible in open palm and reward from other hand when dog leaves it.
steps.rewardTiming: Treat from other hand after successful leave.
steps.progressCriteria: Leaves visible palm item on cue.
steps.easierIfStruggling: Close hand if dog moves toward palm treat.

protocols.generalisationMaintenance: Practice with safe household items before real hazards.
safetyPrecautions: Pair with fair-trade if item already in mouth (see Dogs Trust leave guidance)
protocols.appProgressionNotes: Complements proto-leave-it-dt; RSPCA has no separate drop page.

protocols.title: Lead reactivity — in-the-moment management (Dogs Trust)
protocols.intendedOutcome: Handler prevents escalation and rewards calm disengagement at safe distance from triggers.
inappropriateWhen: Biting or severe aggression without professional plan
protocols.environment: Start on quiet routes; avoid peak dog traffic initially.
protocols.baselineAssessment: Vet check completed for pain/medical contributors.

steps.instruction: Identify triggers and choose quieter walk times/places; turn away or use visual barriers before dog reaches threshold.
steps.rewardTiming: Optional calm praise for successful avoidance.
steps.progressCriteria: Fewer full-threshold reactions on familiar route.

steps.instruction: Keep lead secure but relaxed; if trigger appears, create distance until dog shows relaxation, then reward with food/praise/toy.
steps.rewardTiming: Reward at first relaxed body language after distance increase.
steps.progressCriteria: Dog accepts rewards and can orient to handler at sub-threshold distances.

steps.instruction: Allow 48–72h recovery after major reactions before challenging walks; contact Dogs Trust Behaviour Support Line or ABTC professional for structured modification if needed.
steps.progressCriteria: Owner has referral contact and adjusted walk plan.
steps.easierIfStruggling: Temporary walk suspension with enrichment at home.

protocols.generalisationMaintenance: Management remains until trained replacement behaviours are proofed with professional plan.
stopConditions: Bites or imminent bite risk—management only with behaviourist/vet
referralRequirements: ABTC Clinical Animal Behaviourist or Veterinary Behaviourist for treatment plans
Dogs Trust Behaviour Support Line for triage
protocols.reviewReason: Management-only protocol; clinical reactivity treatment out of app scope.
protocols.appProgressionNotes: Good Dog should surface referral CTAs, not promise cure via management alone.

protocols.title: Puppy socialisation — positive exposure checklist (Dogs Trust)
protocols.intendedOutcome: Puppy forms positive associations with everyday people, animals, sounds, surfaces and objects during the early socialisation window.
inappropriateWhen: Puppy showing sustained fear—pause and seek professional guidance
protocols.environment: Home first; public ground only after vet clearance.

steps.instruction: Begin at home with gentle handling, household sounds (e.g. vacuum off then on at distance), varied surfaces and props (hats, umbrellas) at puppy's pace with rewards for relaxed behaviour.
steps.progressCriteria: Puppy accepts novel home stimuli without fleeing.
steps.easierIfStruggling: Increase distance; reduce duration; split stimuli.

steps.instruction: Before full vaccination, carry puppy to observe people, traffic and dogs from safe distance; reward calm observation.
After vaccination clearance, introduce walks, varied dogs/animals at distance, visitors and sound desensitisation; stop immediately if puppy becomes worried or over-aroused.
steps.progressCriteria: Growing confidence across checklist categories without shutdown.
steps.easierIfStruggling: Return to earlier step; consult vet/trainer.

protocols.generalisationMaintenance: Continue novel experiences through adolescence at sub-threshold levels.
safetyPrecautions: Follow vet vaccination and parasite advice
referralRequirements: Puppy class with reward-based ABTC instructor optional
protocols.reviewReason: Vaccination timing varies by vet; checklist must stay advisory.

behaviours.name: Calm or recoverable at sub-threshold distance from trigger
behaviours.observableCriteria: At handler-chosen distance from trigger, dog can accept food/toy, orient to handler, or show relaxed body language without lunging/barking for at least 3 seconds.

behaviours.name: Relaxed exposure to novel stimulus
behaviours.observableCriteria: Puppy approaches or observes novel person/object/sound at chosen distance with loose body, willing to take treats or engage in play within 30 seconds.

lessons.title: Help your reactive dog on walks
lessons.summary: Create distance, keep the lead relaxed, reward calm—and get vet and behaviour support when needed.

lessons.title: Socialise your puppy safely
lessons.summary: Go at your puppy's pace, keep experiences positive, and follow your vet's guidance before walks on the ground.

lessons.title: Teach leave (RSPCA method)
lessons.summary: Reward your dog for backing away from something so leaving it feels safe and worthwhile.
